newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bars entry of South African union members.
newsitem.headline: Manila bars entry of South African union members.

text.p: The Philippines, determined to prevent disruptions at this month's APEC summit at any cost, barred entry on Tuesday to two South African union leaders who say they had planned to attend an international meeting.
"We are making arrangements to deport the two South Africans immediately due to their doubtful intentions," immigration official Danilo Perez told reporters.

Philippine officials say they are determined to prevent any threat to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit on November 25 to be attended by U.S. President Bill Clinton and other regional leaders.

They earlier refused an entry visa to 1996 Nobel Peace Prize co-winner Jose Ramos-Horta, a leader of the East Timor independence movement, and have pledged to keep out any other potential foreign troublemakers.

One of the two South Africans, Luyanda Makupula, 33, told immigration agents that he and his colleague, Baca Tembinkosi, had been invited to attend an "Anti-Imperialist World Peasant Summit" in Manila from November 10 to 25.
His remarks were contained in a statement to immigration officials, who released a copy to reporters.
Perez, head of the Bureau of Immigration and Deportation's travel control service at Manila international airport, said the two refused to divulge who the organisers of the meeting were.
In his statement, Makupula said the meeting's organisers had contacted them via fax.

The peasants' meeting is organised by the leftist Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas (KMP, Farmers' Movement of the Philippines) and is one of several events being organised by non-government groups to coincide with the 18-member APEC summit and a meeting of APEC foreign ministers on November 22 and 23.
The KMP immediately denounced the deportations.

"The peasant summit is a legitimate venue by which the people can make their voices heard on crucial issues to be tackled in the APEC Subic meeting," Movement chairman Rafael Mariano said in a statement.
"Why stifle this initiative from the grassroots," he said.
The movement said the two union leaders were from the South African Agricultural Plantation Workers' Union, which was affiliated with President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress.
They are being held at the airport and are to be deported back to South Africa on Wednesday.
